Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

equal to zero, so the system becomes invariant.

Key details

  • What does it mean?
  • That we can neither change the temperature nor the pressure.
  • Another point of importance is A, which is known as the critical point.
  • At the point A the interface between the liquid water and the water vapor vanishes.
  • That means we cannot distinguish between the liquid water and the water vapor.
  • Such a point is known as the critical point.
  • Of course this plot is not made to scale because we are using different pressure units.
  • In fact we have even used different units for pressure.
  • When water is cooled below the triple point, it is supposed to get converted into ice.
  • But under certain conditions, it is found that water continues to be in the liquid phase and does not get converted into ice.
  • This is known as super cooled water and it represents a metastable equilibrium.
  • Which involves the liquid and the vapor phases.
  • It is called metastable equilibrium because even a small disturbance is going to cause the system to go back to the stable equilibrium which is represented by the line OB.
  • The vapor pressure of the system now in the metastable region is higher than that of the stable system of ice at the same temperature.
  • And therefore, we find that the line OA prime is always shown above that of the sublimation curve.
  • We know that the phase rule is F is equal to C minus P plus 2.
  • But in the case of a two component system, we will not be able to use this ordinary phase rule.
  • The reason being that.
  • Since C is equal to two here, F is going to be four minus P.
  • One phase then F becomes equal to three.
  • So that means there are three degrees of freedom.
  • Most of the time it is assumed that pressure is constant because we carry out measurements at atmospheric pressure.
  • The new rule, therefore, is F is equal to C minus P plus one.
  • And this is known as the reduced phase rule.
  • The name is derived from the fact that we have reduced the degree of freedom by one because we are assuming.
  • That one of the variables is constant.
  • And this is mostly applicable to solid liquid equilibria because in this case the pressure changes.
  • Will not affect the equilibrium to a great extent as compared to when there would be a gas phase present in the system.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us discuss the metastable equilibrium represented by the line OA prime on this graph.
  • Let us talk about the phase diagram of a two component system.
  • We consider one of the three variables to be constant.
